active_prompts.topic: Did asteroid delivery materially improve the odds of life beginning on early Earth, or did Bennu merely preserve ingredients Earth could make for itself?
angles: Start with the practical causal test: abundance, delivery flux, atmospheric-entry survival, chemical availability and comparison with plausible terrestrial production.
Use current primary OSIRIS-REx sample-analysis papers and official mission documentation, and distinguish pristine returned material from meteorites exposed to Earth.
Compare Bennu with independent Hayabusa2 Ryugu sample results and carbonaceous meteorites, auditing overlapping teams and methods rather than treating every paper as replication.

Trace the history from panspermia to prebiotic-feedstock delivery, including Miller-Urey as a terrestrial alternative, Murchison's contamination problem and ALH84001 as a caution against overinterpreting suggestive extraterrestrial material.

Separate amino acids, nucleobases, ammonia, sugars and ancient-brine minerals from evidence of life. Explain isotope ratios, chirality, racemic mixtures and contamination controls before relying on them.
Include important sceptical or opposing primary work on abiotic formation, atmospheric-entry survival, delivery quantities and early-Earth availability.
Treat very recent sugar or related findings as provisional unless the full primary paper and independent scrutiny are available.
End with measurements that could discriminate the competing accounts, including isotopes, chirality, cross-laboratory aliquot analysis and samples from chemically distinct bodies.
